comments.text:
I would ordinarily say, that the UK Treasury should get the lion's share of any oil windfall. (as the Uk defended it in 82 and that cost the Uk a boatload) However, seeing as they are too dumb to stop an Israeli firm from essentially buying the rights, making the same error they did in the 70s and 80s with North sea oil & gas, and seeing as the UK gov would just give the money away to bs schemes, waste and welfare for migrants, I guess it's best they get none. 

I also guess that Israel go the deal because Milei won't fuck around with Israeli-backed drilling, as he loves those guys. So in that way, getting an Israeli company to buy it was probably diplomatically smart, but I still hate the idea and think the Falklands should partner with someone to fund it jointly. The tax revenue is good, but owning it is essential. 

3 x the island's economy doesn't sound right. Should be far more than that if well structured tbh. 500 million barrels is probably worth 40~ billion USd minus capex, financing (bonds) and op ex. say 15 billion over say 25 years. means 1 billion revenue from sales per year. So that's 500k per person per year x 25 years = 12.5 million USd per Falklander gross . Not bad really. I'm sure the war cost about that per person too in 2026 dollars. I'm also pretty sure they'll find more oil and gas and if they start a wealth fund, that will be quite a big pie in 25 years time.

comments.text: 500 million barrels of oil does not necessarily make this discovery economic and it is way too small to entice the big corporations to invest. I suspect expectations are currently well in excess of future realizations. I understand from Rockhopper’s website that they believe they discovered about 1.7 billion barrels of oil in place and they predicted that 500 million barrels could be extracted at a 50% confidence level (2C). It is interesting, however, that Rockhopper farmed out their interest to Premier Oil, a moderately successful E&P company who could easily have raised the capital to develop this resource. They, however, decided to pull the plug and sold out to an Israeli company. Wonder why? Was it political risk, or the fact that the reservoirs are too segmented and partitioned? Once you get into actual oil recovery mechanisms, how much primary production is expected before secondary methods much be applied to produce the 2C reserves? What will be done with the associated gas produced along with the oil? Will it have to be flared (carbon pollution) or re-injected (additional up front Capital investment)? 140 miles offshore in a pretty hostile sea with an FPSO……..good luck to them I say!
